findings.problem: The plan relies on a loop that sleeps 60 seconds and promises that the first post-midnight run begins on time, but the cited spec schedules crawl-run through launchd every 15 minutes; overlapping firings exit due to the run lock. The plan explicitly leaves the loop/scheduler out of scope, so the proposed engine-only change cannot provide or verify that promise. After a window is cut off at midnight, the next run may not begin until the next scheduled firing.
findings.suggestion: Either limit the outcome and acceptance test to the next scheduled run after the day boundary, or include a deliberate scheduler/loop change and update the scheduling specification so a post-reset run is actually guaranteed.

summary: The plan’s core post-midnight timing guarantee conflicts with the specified scheduler and is out of scope.
